agree.reason: The two commissioners focused on traffic get a concrete fix (a signal paid for by the builder that keeps the intersection at C, made a condition of the permit), so they have a clear reason to vote yes, though neighbours who oppose the project may still object to 20 months of trucks and the busier road.

honest.reason: Every figure traces to the facts, and the speech says plainly that it can't promise traffic won't get worse; the one overstatement is 'You won't find a site that asks less of a neighborhood,' which the facts can't prove.

works_the_facts.reason: The speech works out that 64 homes is about one in six of the 412 households waiting, that 310 trips is about five per household, and that 72 spaces is more than one per home, though it could also have said the project fills about 3% of the county's 2,100-home shortfall.

right_comparison.reason: A no vote is described accurately (the lot stays empty six days a week and 412 households keep waiting about three years), and a yes vote with the signal accurately keeps the C rating, though nothing in the facts shows whether the waiting list is growing.

qualification.reason: The main condition, a signal at Alder and 4th required by the permit with the study saying it keeps the C rating, is specific and checkable, but it has no deadline, such as having the signal in before the units open.

objections.reason: The speech answers traffic, parking and construction trucks with commitments that already exist, and Margaret's own morning backups give the traffic answer credibility, without raising any worry the facts don't already answer.

fit.reason: At about 430 words in plain spoken style, it fits the 3-minute limit for public comment and ends by asking for exactly what Margaret wants.
